div.head: V As 3[a]
div.ab: And mon singe ylce Frigdæge æt ylcum mynstre ealle ða Goddes þeowas an fiftig sealmas for ðone cyng ⁊ for ealle ða ðe willen þæt he wille ⁊ for ða oþre, swa hi swa geearnigen.
⁊ man singe ælc Frigdæge æt ælcum mynstre ealle þa Godes þeowan an fiftig for þone cyng ⁊ for ealle þe willaþ ðæt he wile ⁊ for þa oþre, swa hy geearnian.
Et decantetur omni die Ueneris in singulis ecclesiis unum quinquagenarium (psalmorum) pro rege et omni populo, qui uult quod ipse.
⁊ man singe ælc Frigdæge æt ælcum mynstre ealle þa Godes þeowan an fiftig [sealmas] for þone cyng ⁊ for ealle þe willaþ ðæt he wile ⁊ for þa oþre, swa hy geearnian.

And in every monastery, all the servants of God shall sing every Friday fifty psalms for the king, and for all who are minded to carry out his wishes. And [they shall sing psalms] for these others according to their merits.
And every Friday at every minster all the servants of God are to sing 50 psalms for the king and for all who desire what he desires, and for the others, as they may deserve.
Und man singe, alle Gottesdiener, jeden Freitag in jeder Stiftskirche einen Funfziger [Psalmen] für den König und für alle, die wollen, was er will, und für die anderen, je wie sie es verdienen.
And let all the servants of God sing, every Friday in every minster, a fifty [of psalms] for the king and for all who will what he wills, and for the others, according as they deserve it.
div.note: In H, the fragment of Æthelstan at Thunresfeld (IV As, see p. 171) follows without a break. In Quadr., III As (the Kentish letter) follows.
